newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL interbank rates steady in dull, thin market.
newsitem.headline: KL interbank rates steady in dull, thin market.

text.p: Interbank rates were steady in the absence of any changes in liquidity or other factors in the thin, post-holiday market, dealers said on Friday.

They said the market was quiet as many dealers were still away on holiday after the Chinese Lunar New Year and Moslem Eid al-Fitr. A holiday mood continued to prevail over the market after a five-day closure of banks from February 7 to 11.
The dealers said the one-week and two-week interbank rate was at 7.50/60 percent and one-month to six-month at 7.35/40 percent, all unchanged from Thursday.

"The market should return to normal next week when everybody comes back to work and funds which had gone out during the festivals would also return to the system," said the head of money dealing at a Malaysian bank.
He said interest rates were expected to ease slightly as funds return to the system over the next two weeks.
An estimated three billion ringgit has temporarily left the banking system, mostly in cash, for the festivals.
